UMCG Groningen Radiology | 05 January 2025 | Multiparametric MRI Prostate
Clinical context: Assessment of elevated PSA (4.3 ng/mL) alongside a previously assigned PI-RADS 2 categorisation. Clinically significant malignancy is being ruled out.

Observations: The gland occupies a volume of 57.0 mL. Both peripheral and transition zones exhibit uniform signal intensity, lacking focal architectural distortion or capsular irregularity. Diffusion-weighted sequences reveal no restricted diffusion across any region, while dynamic contrast-enhanced series show no early or focal enhancement. Seminal vesicles appear normal and symmetrical. The visualised pelvis demonstrates no suspicious lymphadenopathy or osseous lesions.

Impression: PI-RADS 2. No lesion graded 3 or higher. Prostate volume 57.0 mL, PSAD 0.07 ng/mL/mL. csPCa predicted probability 0.2787341.

previous_notes.author: Dr. L. Smits (GP)
previous_notes.text: Surveillance review documented earlier measurements of 3.0 ng/mL in June 2022 and 2.8 ng/mL in May 2023, both considered appropriate for his age bracket. Monitoring continued without urgent intervention or procedural steps at that time.
